fieldMarks: Horny rattle on the tail tip; broad head and vertical pupil in bright light
Heat-sensing pit on each side of the face between eye and nostril
Almost always dark crossbands on a yellow, black or gray background, sometimes a reddish mid-back stripe
Heavy-bodied with keeled scales and a coarse, dull skin; usually under 150 cm
behavior: Emerges from dens about mid-April to May and returns about mid-September to October
Northern and upland snakes hibernate communally; males typically stay within 3.6 km of the den
Eats mainly small mammals; lizards in the south
habitat: Northeast: hilly forest with rocky outcrops and ledges; Midwest: rocky bluffs; South: hardwood forest, river bottoms and swampy areas.
range: Central New England to northern Florida, west to eastern Texas, central Oklahoma, eastern Kansas, southeastern Nebraska, Iowa and southeastern Minnesota; spotty at the western and northern edges. NatureServe ranks it NX (presumed extirpated) in Canada.
